stories.title: Insulin product in short supply after German manufacturer halts supplies, NA told
summary: An insulin product used by patients with Type 1 diabetes is in short supply in Pakistan after its German manufacturer halted supplies while upgrading its products, Parliamentary Secretary for Health Nelson Azeem said on Friday.

She said the alternatives were at least 20 per cent more expensive and that many patients did not have access to doctors. “Currently, around 34.5 million people in Pakistan have Type 1 diabetes, including children,” she said. “Alternatives are not readily available.

In August 2025, the Pakistan Medical Association raised alarm over “an unprecedented” and severe shortage of essential medicines across the country and warned that the crisis threatened the lives of millions of patients.

stories.title: New Greece law bans social media for under-15s
summary: Greece’s parliament passed a law on Friday banning children under 15 from social media, joining a growing number of countries imposing curbs on young people’s use of the apps.

Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis announced plans for the ban in April, taking to TikTok — one of the most popular social networks with young people in Greece — to explain the “difficult but necessary” measure.
The opposition socialist Pasok party abstained after seeking an alternative bill that would have banned social media for under-13s and parental controls for 13- and 14-year-olds.

stories.title: China orders 'all-out' rescue after Tibet quake kills 16
summary: China ordered an “all-out” rescue effort in Tibet on Friday after an earthquake killed at least 16 people, injured dozens and flattened hundreds of homes, state media reported.
The disaster came little over a year after at least 148 people died in a quake in remote Gansu province in northwest China in December 2023, according to state media.
That quake was China’s deadliest since 2014, when more than 600 people perished in the southwestern province of Yunnan.

stories.title: Taiwan shuts down ahead of Typhoon Champi, nearly 1,000 flights cancelled
summary: Almost all of Taiwan shut down on Friday ahead of the arrival of Typhoon Champi, which is forecast to bring strong winds and torrential rain, and though the storm is weakening it could still make direct landfall on the island.

At one point a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the Pacific this year, Champi was still packing gusts of around 191 kph near its centre, according to Taiwan’s Central Weather Administration (CWA).

A fisherman walks among fishing nets at a fishing port as Typhoon Champi approaches Taiwan, in Keelung, Taiwan on October 23, 2026. —Reuters The transport ministry said all 262 domestic flights were cancelled for Friday, along with 717 international ones.
